title: Noir
description: Noir, the noir preset look, is wet streets, venetian gobos, and a crime already in the lighting: a motivated hard key, black pools, a face half-deleted. Night is moral, and a dark photo with teal is not this.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Crime, conscience, a city that judges: one practical in the deep, smoke optional, contrast as law. The viral-named version of film-noir grammar.
It can stay silver, or go wet neon if you say so. A sitcom kitchen does not want venetian blinds unless the joke is noir.
It is the wrong tool when the key is soft and the blacks are mush. That is moody, not noir.
If you wanted color-era melancholy, say neo-noir.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Noir in film?
A named night recipe: wet streets, venetian gobos, hard motivated key, crime already in the lighting. It is contrast law, not a dark LUT.
Noir vs Neo-Noir
Film noir and this preset can stay silver. Neo-noir retools the same guilt in color and later tech. If you want neon melancholy, say neo-noir. If you want gobos and wet black, this is the recipe.
When should I use Noir?
Crime, conscience, a judging city. Skip sitcom kitchens and soft dark grades.
How do I prompt Noir for AI image or video?
Hard key, wet street, then: Noir look on [Subject], wet streets, venetian gobos, a crime already in the lighting. Keep contrast as law. Do not add teal mush.
